L00011: L00012: # BixBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for LLM-based Agents in Computational Biology L00013: L00014: BixBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on real-world bioinformatics tasks. L00015: This benchmark tests AI agents' ability to: L00016: L00017: - Explore biological datasets L00018: - Perform long, multi-step computational analyses L00019: - Interpret nuanced results in the context of a research question L00020: L00021: BixBench presents AI agents with open-ended or multiple-choice tasks, requiring them to navigate datasets, execute code (Python, R, Bash), generate scientific hypotheses, and validate them. L00022: The dataset contains 205 questions derived from 60 real-world, published Jupyter notebooks and related data (capsules). L00023: L00024: You can find the BixBench dataset on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench), read details in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00096), and read our [blog post announcement](https://www.futurehouse.org/research-announcements/bixbench). L00025: L00026: This repository enables three separate functions: L00027: L00028: 1. Agentic evaluations of LLMs on BixBench L00029: 2. Zero-shot evaluations of LLMs on BixBench L00030: 3. Replicating the BixBench paper results L00031: L00032: ## Links L00033: L00034: - [Installation](#installation) L00035: - [Quick Start](#quick-start) L00036: - [Agentic Evaluations](#agentic-evaluations) L00037: - [Using Your Own Agent](#using-your-own-agent) L00038: - [Zero-shot Evaluations & Grading](#zero-shot-evaluations--grading) L00039: - [Replicating the BixBench Paper Results](#replicating-the-bixbench-paper-results) L00040: - [Acknowledgments](#acknowledgments) L00041: L00042: ## Installation L00043: L00044: To set up the repository, first clone it and install the dependencies: L00045: L00046: ```bash L00047: # Clone the repository L00048: git clone https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench.git L00049: cd BixBench L00050: L00051: # Install dependencies L00052: pip install -e . # or `uv sync` if you are using uv L00053: ``` L00054: L00055: Next, you will need to be able to access the BixBench dataset. To do this, you will have to authenticate with Hugging Face: L00056: L00057: ```bash L00058: # Authenticate with Hugging Face L00059: huggingface-cli login L00060: ``` L00061: L00062: See the [Hugging Face CLI](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/en/guides/cli) for how to get started with the Hugging Face CLI and [Hugging Face Security Tokens](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/en/guides/security-tokens) for more information on how to create a token. L00063: L00064: Finally, the agent executes its data analysis code in a containerized environment. So to run it, you will need to pull the docker image: L00065: L00066: ```bash L00067: # Pull the docker image L00068: docker pull futurehouse/bixbench:aviary-notebook-env L00069: ``` L00070: L00071: See [Docker's Getting Started Guide](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/) for instructions on how to set up Docker. L00072: L00073: ## Quick Start L00074: L00075: For quick reproduction of BixBench results, we provide automated scripts that handle the entire evaluation pipeline: L00076: L00077: ### Option 1: Automated Evaluation (Recommended) L00078: L00079: ```bash L00080: # Run zero-shot evaluations and grading (fastest) L00081: bash scripts/run_zeroshot.sh L00082: L00083: # Run agentic evaluations with multiple replicas (takes 24-48 hours) L00084: bash scripts/run_agentic.sh L00085: ``` L00086: L00087: ### Option 2: Manual Configuration L00088: L00089: ```bash L00090: # Generate trajectories with specific configuration L00091: python bixbench/generate_trajectories.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/4o_image.yaml L00092: L00093: # Run postprocessing to generate results L00094: python bixbench/postprocessing.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/v1.5_paper_results.yaml L00095: ``` L00096: L00097: ⚠️ **Note**: The automated agentic evaluation script will run multiple models (GPT-4o, Claude) across 5 replicas each, which requires significant API credits and 24-48 hours to complete. L00098: L00099: ## Prerequisites L00100: L00101: ### API Keys L00102: L00103: We support all LLMs that are supported by [litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm). Create a `.env` file with the API keys for the LLMs you want to evaluate. For example: L00104: L00105: ```env L00106: OPENAI_API_KEY = "your-openai-api-key" L00107: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "your-anthropic-api-key" L00108: ``` L00109: L00110: ## Agentic Evaluations L00111: L00112: BixBench evaluates agents' ability to create complex Jupyter notebooks for real-world bioinformatics research questions. To evaluate an LLM on BixBench we separate the process into two steps: L00113: L00114: 1. Generate trajectories L00115: 2. Evaluate the trajectories via postprocessing L00116: L00117: ### Generate Trajectories L00118: L00119: BixBench evaluates agents' ability to create complex Jupyter notebooks for real-world bioinformatics research questions. To generate these trajectories, it's as simple as configuring a YAML file and running the following command: L00120: L00121: ```bash L00122: python bixbench/generate_trajectories.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/generate_trajectories.yaml L00123: ``` L00124: L00125: This will: L00126: L00127: 1. Download the BixBench dataset from Hugging Face (only needed once) L00128: 2. Preprocess each capsule in the dataset L00129: 3. Generate and store trajectories including the final agent answer and Jupyter notebook in the directory specified in the YAML file L00130: L00131: Trajectories are saved in the specified `trajectories_dir` in the YAML file as json files (default is `data/trajectories/`). L00132: L00133: ### Customization L00134: L00135: Edit or create a new YAML file to modify: L00136: L00137: - Model configurations L00138: - System prompts L00139: - Batch sizes L00140: - File paths L00141: - Evaluation modes L00142: - Rollout configuration L00143: L00144: ### Using Your Own Agent L00145: L00146: To use your own agent, use the `generate_trajectories.py` script by editing the [`custom_rollout`](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/6c28217959d5d7dd6f48c59894534fced7c6c040/bixbench/generate_trajectories.py#L239) function to generate trajectories in the same format as the BixBench trajectories, then use the `postprocessing.py` script to evaluate your agent's performance. L00147: L00148: ### Evaluate trajectories L00149: L00150: Similarly, to evaluate the trajectories, we use the `postprocessing.py` script alongside a YAML configuration file: L00151: L00152: ```bash L00153: python bixbench/postprocessing.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/postprocessing.yaml L00154: ``` L00155: L00156: This script will: L00157: L00158: 1. Load the raw trajectory data L00159: 2. Create an evaluation dataframe L00160: 3. Run majority vote analysis (for MCQ questions) L00161: 4. Compare model performance across different run groups defined in the YAML file L00162: 5. Generate visualizations L00163: L00164: The script will save the evaluation dataframe as a CSV file in the `bixbench_results/` directory as well as the plots. L00165: L00166: ## Zero-shot Evaluations & Grading L00167: L00168: You can run zero-shot evaluations using the `generate_zeroshot_evals.py` script and then grade the responses using the `grade_outputs.py` script. These two scripts: L00169: L00170: 1. Loads the BixBench dataset from Hugging Face L00171: 2. Evaluates the LLM on the dataset, outputting a CSV file with the results L00172: 3. Grades the responses using LLM-based graders for open-ended answer or exact match for MCQs L00173: 4. Saves the final results as a JSON file L00174: L00175: The scripts can be configured to run with open-ended questions, multiple-choice questions (with or without a refusal option), different models, and different temperatures. To explore the different options, run the scripts with the `--help` flag. L00176: L00177: ### Example: Generate zero-shot answers in MCQ setting with the "refusal option" (in addition to the original distractors) L00178: L00179: ```bash L00180: python generate_zeroshot_evals.py \ L00181: --answer-mode "mcq" \ L00182: --model "gpt-4o" \ L00183: --with-refusal L00184: ``` L00185: L00186: ### Example: Grade the zero-shot answers from the previous step L00187: L00188: ```bash L00189: python grade_outputs.py \ L00190: --input-file path/to/zeroshot.csv \ L00191: --answer-mode "mcq" L00192: ``` L00193: L00194: ## Replicating the BixBench Paper Results L00195: L00196: ### v1.5 Results (Latest) L00197: L00198: For the latest BixBench v1.5 results using the enhanced 205-question dataset, use the automated scripts or the v1.5 configuration: L00199: L00200: #### Quick Reproduction L00201: L00202: ```bash L00203: # Complete reproduction using automation scripts L00204: bash scripts/run_zeroshot.sh # Zero-shot baselines L00205: bash scripts/run_agentic.sh # Agentic evaluations (24-48 hours) L00206: ``` L00207: L00208: #### Manual v1.5 Reproduction L00209: L00210: ```bash L00211: # Generate v1.5 results L00212: python bixbench/postprocessing.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/v1.5_paper_results.yaml L00213: ``` L00214: L00215: The v1.5 configuration includes: L00216: L00217: - **Majority vote analysis** with k=5 replicas L00218: - **Image comparison analysis** (with/without image support) L00219: - **Refusal option comparison** (with/without refusal options in MCQs) L00220: - **Zero-shot baseline integration** for comprehensive model comparison L00221: - **Updated result paths** using `bixbench-v1.5_results/` directory structure L00222: L00223: ### Original Paper Results L00224: L00225: To replicate the original BixBench paper results, you can download the raw data from 2,120 trajectories and its respective postprocessed evaluation dataframe: L00226: L00227: ```bash L00228: wget https://storage.googleapis.com/bixbench-results/raw_trajectory_data.csv -P bixbench_results/ L00229: wget https://storage.googleapis.com/bixbench-results/eval_df.csv -P bixbench_results/ L00230: ``` L00231: L00232: You can then run the postprocessing script to generate the evaluation dataframe and analysis plots using the original configuration file: L00233: L00234: ```bash L00235: python bixbench/postprocessing.py --config_file bixbench/run_configuration/bixbench_paper_results.yaml L00236: ``` L00237: L00238: ### Generated Figures L00239: L00240: The evaluation process will generate the following comparative visualizations: L00241: L00242: **v1.5 Results:** L00243: L00244: You will see the following figures from the paper: L00245: ![Performance Comparison](bixbench-v1.5_results/bixbench_results_comparison.png) L00246: L00247: ![Majority Vote Accuracy](bixbench-v1.5_results/majority_vote_accuracy_refusal_option_comparison.png) L00248: L00249: **Original Results:** L00250: L00251: - `bixbench_results/bixbench_results_comparison.png` - Original performance comparison L00252: - `bixbench_results/majority_vote_accuracy_refusal_option_comparison.png` - Original majority vote analysis L00253: L00254: ## Gotchas L00255: L00256: - The BixBench dataset is large and may take several minutes to download. L00257: - **API Costs**: The automated agentic evaluation script (`run_agentic.sh`) will incur significant API costs as it runs 5 replicas across multiple model configurations (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet). Estimate your costs before running. L00258: - **Execution Time**: Complete agentic evaluations take 24-48 hours. Use the zero-shot script (`run_zeroshot.sh`) for faster results if you only need baseline comparisons. L00259: - When generating trajectories manually, the default batch size is set to 4 to optimize processing speed. You may need to adjust this value in the [configuration file](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/8c57d3562044e4ce574a09438066033e21155f54/bixbench/run_configuration/generate_trajectories.yaml#L14) based on your API rate limits and available compute resources. L00260: - While the agent can use a local Jupyter kernel, we recommend using our custom Docker environment for improved performance (default is `USE_DOCKER=true`). Be sure to pull the Docker image as described in the [Installation](#installation) section. If you would like to use a local Jupyter kernel, set use_docker to false in the notebook section of the configuration file. L00261: - **Directory Structure**: The v1.5 automation scripts create and use `bixbench-v1.5_results/` while manual configurations may use `bixbench_results/` or other directories as specified in the YAML files. L00262: L00263: ## Acknowledgments L00264: L00265: BixBench is the product of a collaboration between [FutureHouse](https://futurehouse.org) and [ScienceMachine](https://www.sciencemachine.ai/).

L00014: class GradeType(StrEnum):
L00015:     CORRECT = "correct"
L00016:     INCORRECT = "incorrect"
L00017:     REFUSED = "refused"
L00018: 
L00019:     @property
L00020:     def numeric_grade(self) -> int:
L00021:         """Convert grade to numeric value."""
L00022:         return 1 if self == GradeType.CORRECT else 0
L00023: 
L00024:     @property
L00025:     def is_correct(self) -> bool:
L00026:         """Check if grade represents a correct answer."""
L00027:         return self == GradeType.CORRECT
L00028: 
L00029:     @property
L00030:     def is_incorrect(self) -> bool:
L00031:         """Check if grade represents a correct answer."""
L00032:         return self == GradeType.INCORRECT
L00033: 
L00034:     @property
L00035:     def is_refused(self) -> bool:
L00036:         """Check if grade represents a refusal."""
L00037:         return self == GradeType.REFUSED
L00038:

L00040: class GradeResult(BaseModel):
L00041:     """Result of grading an answer."""
L00042: 
L00043:     grade: int = Field(ge=0, le=1, description="Numeric grade (0 or 1)")
L00044:     correct: bool = Field(description="Whether the answer is correct")
L00045:     refusal: bool = Field(description="Whether the answer is a refusal")
L00046:     grade_type: GradeType | None = Field(default=None, description="Type of grade")
L00047:     raw_response: str | None = Field(
L00048:         default=None, description="Raw LLM response for open-ended"
L00049:     )
L00050: 
L00051:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
L00052:         return {"grade": self.grade, "correct": self.correct, "refusal": self.refusal}
L00053: 
L00054: 
L00055: class GradingFunction(BaseModel):
L00056:     """Base class for grading functions."""
L00057: 
L00058:     def _parse_grade_response(self, response: str) -> GradeType:
L00059:         """Parse the grade from LLM response."""
L00060:         match = re.search(r"<grade>\s*(.*?)\s*</grade>", response, re.DOTALL)
L00061:         grade = match[1].strip().lower() if match else None
L00062: 
L00063:         return GradeType.CORRECT if grade == "correct" else GradeType.INCORRECT
L00064: 
L00065:     async def _grade_str_verifier(
L00066:         self,
L00067:         target,
L00068:         predicted,
L00069:         unsure=None,
L00070:         question=None,
L00071:         partial_match=False,
L00072:         llm_match=False,
L00073:         llm_client=None,
L00074:         grading_prompt_template=OPEN_ENDED_GRADING_PROMPT,
L00075:     ) -> GradeResult:
L00076:         # normalize the target and predicted answers
L00077:         # EXACT match grading
L00078:         cleaned_target = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "", target).lower()
L00079:         cleaned_predicted = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "", predicted).lower()
L00080: 
L00081:         correct = cleaned_predicted == cleaned_target
L00082:         refusal = predicted == unsure if unsure else False
L00083:         if not correct and partial_match:
L00084:             # PARTIAL match grading
L00085:             correct = cleaned_predicted in cleaned_target
L00086:             if not correct and llm_match:
L00087:                 # LLM verifier grading
L00088:                 return await self._grade_llm_verifier(
L00089:                     question=question,
L00090:                     target=target,
L00091:                     predicted=predicted,
L00092:                     llm_client=llm_client,
L00093:                     grading_prompt_template=grading_prompt_template,
L00094:                 )
L00095: 
L00096:         if correct:
L00097:             grade_type = GradeType.CORRECT
L00098:         elif refusal:
L00099:             grade_type = GradeType.REFUSED
L00100:         else:
L00101:             grade_type = GradeType.INCORRECT
L00102: 
L00103:         return GradeResult(
L00104:             grade=grade_type.numeric_grade,
L00105:             correct=grade_type.is_correct,
L00106:             refusal=grade_type.is_refused,  # this is only for mcq grading
L00107:             grade_type=grade_type,
L00108:         )
L00109: 
L00110:     async def _grade_llm_verifier(
L00111:         self,
L00112:         question: str,
L00113:         target: str,
L00114:         predicted: str,
L00115:         llm_client: LiteLLMModel,
L00116:         grading_prompt_template=OPEN_ENDED_GRADING_PROMPT,
L00117:     ) -> GradeResult:
L00118:         grading_query = grading_prompt_template.format(
L00119:             question=question, target=target, predicted=predicted
L00120:         )
L00121:         completion = await llm_client.call_single([Message(content=grading_query)])
L00122:         response = completion.text or ""
L00123:         grade_type = self._parse_grade_response(response)
L00124: 
L00125:         return GradeResult(
L00126:             grade=grade_type.numeric_grade,
L00127:             correct=grade_type.is_correct,
L00128:             refusal=grade_type.is_refused,
L00129:             grade_type=grade_type,
L00130:             raw_response=response,
L00131:         )
L00132: 
L00133:     async def _grade_range_llm_verifier(
L00134:         self,
L00135:         question,
L00136:         target: str,
L00137:         predicted: str,
L00138:         llm_client: LiteLLMModel,
L00139:         grading_prompt_template=OPEN_ENDED_RANGE_GRADING_PROMPT,
L00140:     ) -> GradeResult:
L00141:         grading_query = grading_prompt_template.format(
L00142:             question=question, target=target, predicted=predicted
L00143:         )
L00144:         completion = await llm_client.call_single([Message(content=grading_query)])
L00145:         response = completion.text or ""
L00146:         grade_type = self._parse_grade_response(response)
L00147: 
L00148:         return GradeResult(
L00149:             grade=grade_type.numeric_grade,
L00150:             correct=grade_type.is_correct,
L00151:             refusal=grade_type.is_refused,
L00152:             grade_type=grade_type,
L00153:         )
L00154: 
L00155:     def _grade_range_verifier(
L00156:         self,
L00157:         target: str,
L00158:         predicted: str,
L00159:     ) -> GradeResult:
L00160:         lower, upper = ast.literal_eval(target)
L00161:         correct = lower <= float(predicted) <= upper
L00162:         if correct:
L00163:             grade_type = GradeType.CORRECT
L00164: 
L00165:         return GradeResult(
L00166:             grade=grade_type.numeric_grade,
L00167:             correct=grade_type.is_correct,
L00168:             refusal=grade_type.is_refused,
L00169:             grade_type=grade_type,
L00170:         )

L00174:     """Grader for multiple choice questions."""

L00184:         self,

L00186:         predicted: str,

L00199:                 llm_match=False,

L00201:         if evaluation_mode == "range_verifier":
L00202:             return grading_func._grade_range_verifier(

L00206:         raise ValueError(f"Unknown eval_mode: {evaluation_mode}")

L00209: class OpenEndedGrader(BaseModel):
L00210:     """Grader for open-ended questions."""
L00211: 
L00212:     evaluation_mode: Literal["llm_verifier", "str_verifier", "range_verifier"] = Field(

L00215:     llm_client: Any = Field(description="LLM client for grading")

L00232:     @model_validator(mode="after")

L00240:         self,
L00241:         question: str,

L00257:                 grading_prompt_template=self.grading_prompt_template,
L00258:             )

L00260:         if self.evaluation_mode == "range_verifier":
L00261:             return await grading_func._grade_range_llm_verifier(
L00262:                 question=question,
L00263:                 target=target,
L00264:                 predicted=predicted,
L00265:                 llm_client=self.llm_client,
L00266:                 grading_prompt_template=self.grading_prompt_template,
L00267:             )
L00268: 
L00269:         if self.evaluation_mode == "llm_verifier":
L00270:             return await grading_func._grade_llm_verifier(
L00271:                 question=question,
L00272:                 target=target,
L00273:                 predicted=predicted,
L00274:                 llm_client=self.llm_client,
L00275:                 grading_prompt_template=self.grading_prompt_template,
